item.title: Re: WarFlying: I busted the Cessna out of storage again late last year after getting the flying bug again and got new 9S batteries for xmas. Managed to get do a repeat of my old 2014 flight but twice and high this time. Went out for an early morning flight yesterday right when there was still zero wind, it would later pick up to 24 mph by noon. Was a fun time got a good amount of mileage in and got an updated scan of what is still there, what isn't, and what's new as well as tons of bluetooth. I had the old gopro session cube on intervalometer under the nose right in front of the forward landing gear and got a few decent propeller free shots. Though I did strike the prop on a rock while landing accidentally, replaced it with a fresh one after I got home. https://i.ibb.co/PGvTxvbk/GOPR0546-1.jpg -Wolfess

Re: WarFlying: Hopping in to re-invigorate a newly necro'd thread, but just today I started putting together the bag of parts to go warflying with a small fixed wing drone, hauling not much more than a Pi Zero W, GPS, and a LoRa link. If I get anywhere at all, I'll be improving the antenna later.How did this work out for you? Also toying with he idea of using a toy quad and a phone or pi0If it has no downlink and you fly visually the original way it would work fine, otherwise the 2.4ghz use on it that close to the phone would severely degrade the reception and you wouldn't get as many networks logged. The DJIs now have a manual band selection and send both the RC and video over the same channel so you could manually set it to use the 5.8ghz band. -Wolfess

Re: WiGLE WiFi for Android phone performance comparison: another comparison, this time all Samsung i have around: S4, S7, S10, S20. I drove with them around town for an good hour behind the windscreen. Data input, wifi count: S4: 6215 S7: 4923 S10: 7725 S20: 8774 And compared against each other: Found by all: 3169 Found only by S4: 616 Found only by S7: 381 Found only by S10: 1111 Found only by S20: 1980 -d2k2
Wifyrda, 14 ESP32-S3, one for each channel: Hello, have you seen the 14 ESP32-S3 module Wifyrda? One for each channel on the 2,4ghz band https://github.com/lozaning/The_Wifydra -d2k2
Re: HardHat Brigade: Love the pineapple setup \m/ -Stratt3000

HardHat Brigade: Hey! I've been wardriving for about a year now, and it has been pretty fun. I've even made it an effort while I am biking around the neighborhood. My two primary devices I've been utilizing is the ATOM GPS Kit, and my Wi-Fi Pineapple Mk7 with a GPS Dongle. I've implemented these devices in various ways, but the one thing I have not built is a hard hat rig. Is there a discord, or a forum post I can reference while I build this thing? If so I would love if someone could DM me a link! I've also been considering switching to Android, so let me know what devices you recommend! If you want to see the tactical pineapple build I made, here is a video of it: https://youtu.be/JFJXNOTMw_E?si=nm3KkpJEppvlD-lp Thanks in advance! -J4YT0RR3S

Re: Best Android for WigleWifi: Go to Walmart and buy a prepaid device (Straight talk/at&t/etc.) for under $50. I bought a Moto G 5g for $40. No need to buy a plan or pay for activation. Battery life is crazy long when you only have 1 or 2 apps installed (besides the oem bloat that I uninstall or disable). -z96Cobra

Wardriving with smartwatches - any advice and recommendations?: Hi, today I thought about trying to install Wigle on a smart watch, specifically the Samsung Galaxy Watch 4, it can be done using wireless debugging. It seems to work, and quite well, the advantage of the watch is its inconspicuousness and at the same time an unobstructed view of the surroundings on the wrist, the only problem is the rate at which the battery drains. Has anyone ever tried Wigle on a watch? Do you have any advice on recommended watches for the best price/performance and battery life? Thanks for answers, it's certainly an interesting topic. -lukaskicz

Re: Temporary laptop / car rig: A little late but On a laptop with a GPS usb, you can use kismet. There is now a wardrive mode, that is more light weight to run, but in whatever mode, this is not a problem on a laptop. I am assuming a Linux OS here, or anyhting that is not Windows ... On a rpi, you can try to run my little app https://github.com/solsticedhiver/ssid-logger. But that requires a minimum of knowledge to get it up and running -zebul666

Re: Best Android for WigleWifi: the S7 is nice (i run 2 on lineageos) but against a S10 its lame. and the S10 you can get for cheap with a broken but working screen. But naming a "best bang for buck" is hard, it all depends on how cheap you are willing to go with the defects -d2k2

Re: Best Android for WigleWifi: According to this user the Samsung Galaxy S7 is the best bang for the buck: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1ibg0tg ... x=9&t=163s That was talready wo years ago and next year this model will celebrate it's 10th anniversary. But the specs are pretty awesome for a phone launched in 2016. It will do trick and you'll only lack Wi-Fi 6 support. Ebay has still a lot to offer, mainly from sellers in the USA or China. I can vouch also for the oneplus 6/6T from 2018 running Android 11. The only downside to it is that you won't have an external SD card slot. -cacheado

Re: Pixel 9 (Pro) its so bad, wow...: Running a bit longer i have mixed results now. Sometimes its ok, but most times its bad Cant see a pattern here, the only thing that realy fixes it for me is keeping the screen on -d2k2

Re: Pixel 9 (Pro) its so bad, wow...: It's still a puzzle - there's a dev branch as I've experimented, but there have been a lot of confusing problems and dead-ends here. Darn it, Pixel team, this "optimization" sucks! -arkasha

Re: Pixel 9 (Pro) its so bad, wow...: 1. under the app battery settings for the WiGLE WiFi Wardriving app, you'll get a single row: "Allow background usage" followed by a toggle. 2. Tap the TEXT (not the toggle!) to get to the second menu, where you can permit the application "Unrestricted" background permission (effectively turning off the now-default "Optimized" behavior) 3. Restart your phone, launch the app, and rock on.I did this now to the P9P and yes it helps a lot. Thanks! With the unrestricted background permission it is about even with a S10. It is still loosing against a S20, but not as much as before. I would have never found this magic second menu, what a hidden thing... -d2k2

Re: Temporary laptop / car rig: for Windows i used ages ago inSSIDer: https://www.metageek.com/inssider/ you need to also connect a GPS. in the end you can upload the logfile directly here. Today, i would run a Kali-VM https://www.kali.org/ and then work with Kismet. -d2k2
